title: SkyWater and D-Wave Extend Quantum Manufacturing Partnership Through Multi-Year Agreement - Quantum Computing Report
gist: D-Wave (QBTS) and SkyWater signed a multi-year extension of their decade-long quantum chip manufacturing collaboration at SkyWater's Minnesota fab, covering annealing and gate-model QPUs. SkyWater remains a merchant foundry for outside quantum developers despite IonQ's acquisition of it.

insights.claim: D-Wave Quantum (Nasdaq: QBTS) and SkyWater Technology signed a multi-year agreement extending their decade-long quantum hardware development and manufacturing collaboration.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Secures D-Wave's fabrication supply chain, reducing manufacturing-continuity risk for its roadmap.

insights.claim: The agreement secures access to specialized process engineering, thin-film fabrication, and semiconductor manufacturing at SkyWater's Minnesota fab, which supports D-Wave's dual-platform roadmap of quantum annealing systems and gate-model quantum computers.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Confirms D-Wave continues funding both annealing and gate-model development rather than abandoning one track.

insights.claim: SkyWater's fabrication has underpinned multiple generations of D-Wave QPUs, including production of its Advantage2 processors, and the deal ensures continuity for Advantage2 and next-generation annealing and gate-model QPUs.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: D-Wave's chip supply depends on a single long-standing foundry relationship, a concentration worth monitoring.

insights.claim: The deal includes proprietary process development terms intended to protect D-Wave's quantum system designs and process IP as chip complexity scales.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: IP terms matter more as foundry-built superconducting chips grow in complexity.

themes.theme: Quantum annealing applied to fab operations

insights.claim: In a proof-of-technology project, D-Wave's quantum annealing algorithms optimized maintenance scheduling at SkyWater's fab and reduced lot delays by up to 30%, increasing factory throughput.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: A claimed 30% delay reduction is a customer-reference-style result for annealing in manufacturing; 'up to' and the lack of classical baseline comparison limit its weight.

insights.claim: An upcoming phase of the SkyWater scheduling project will expand the model to incorporate technician availability and complex operational constraints.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Follow-on phase could convert the proof of technology into a recurring commercial use case.

insights.claim: Following IonQ's acquisition of SkyWater Technology and the launch of the SkyWater Quantum Solutions division, the contract extension confirms SkyWater continues to operate as a merchant foundry for external quantum hardware developers.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Neutrality of a foundry now owned by a competitor is a key risk for outside quantum developers; this deal is evidence it is being maintained.
